decisions.reason: Simultaneous dual-station operation does not change the existing motor-speed range or maximum-speed constraints; the separate request to demonstrate speed adjustment is not part of the source Event's value change.

The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY for continuous operation, and its existing electrical-load requirement already covers both motors operating under load. The simultaneous-operation decision adds no necessary candidate-state change.
Requiring both stations to operate simultaneously does not itself alter the established splash-control behavior or methods.
Simultaneous station operation does not change whisk-removal, cleaning, or tool-free detachment requirements.
The source decision does not change whisk-head size, material, style, compatibility, or positioning.
Operating both stations simultaneously does not modify the required smoothness, froth, consistency, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The simultaneous-operation decision is unrelated to the deferred accent-lighting requirement.

The source Event changes dual-station operation, not dispensing-flow quality. The message's separate request to demonstrate both spouts does not alter the existing smooth, controlled dispensing criteria.

The candidate already requires leak-free liquid containment across the plumbing system. Simultaneous station operation does not change that state, while the leak-repair and leak-free demonstration clauses are separate from the source Event's value change.
The simultaneous-operation requirement does not necessarily revise the approved BOM or its documented component-selection obligations.
Simultaneous operation of the two stations does not change bowl capacity, form, refilling, or size-selection priorities.
Although simultaneous operation may exercise the structure, the client does not change the existing stability or vibration-control criteria in this source decision.
